title: Suppliers With No Orders Since June 1998 (NOT EXISTS vs NOT IN)
outcome: 🆕 new practice question — not attempted yet
watchOutFor: NOT IN returns no rows if the subquery yields a NULL; NOT EXISTS has no such trap and plans as an anti-join.
problem: Procurement wants to review suppliers whose products haven't been ordered since 1 June 1998.
objective: List suppliers none of whose products appear on an order dated on or after 1998-06-01, by supplier id.
expectedOutput:
| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| supplier_id | Supplier |
| company_name | Supplier name |

| supplier_id | company_name |
|-------------|--------------|
| 1 | Exotic Liquids |
| 5 | Cooperativa de Quesos |
| 7 | Pavlova, Ltd. |
| 12 | Plutzer Lebensmittel |

*(Sample rows are illustrative — the first few rows from the practice dataset, shown to convey shape/format; your data instance may differ.)*
approach:
1. For each supplier, look for any order line of their products with order_date >= '1998-06-01'.
2. Keep suppliers where that search finds nothing (NOT EXISTS).
3. Order by supplier_id.
mySolution:
SELECT s.supplier_id, s.company_name
FROM suppliers s
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM products p
    JOIN order_details d ON d.product_id = p.product_id
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = d.order_id
    WHERE p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
      AND o.order_date >= DATE '1998-06-01'
)
ORDER BY s.supplier_id;
solution:
SELECT s.supplier_id, s.company_name
FROM suppliers s
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM products p
    JOIN order_details d ON d.product_id = p.product_id
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = d.order_id
    WHERE p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
      AND o.order_date >= DATE '1998-06-01'
)
ORDER BY s.supplier_id;
referenceQuery:
SELECT s.supplier_id, s.company_name
FROM suppliers s
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM products p
    JOIN order_details d ON d.product_id = p.product_id
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = d.order_id
    WHERE p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
      AND o.order_date >= DATE '1998-06-01'
)
ORDER BY s.supplier_id;
why: An anti-join keeps rows with no match. NOT EXISTS expresses it directly and PostgreSQL plans it as a hash or merge anti-join. The equivalent NOT IN (SELECT supplier_id …) silently returns nothing if any value in the subquery is NULL, because x NOT IN (…, NULL) is never true. The date is compared as a plain range on the column, so an index on order_date can be used.
pitfalls: NOT IN with a nullable subquery column, which can return zero rows.
Filtering with EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 1998 AND EXTRACT(MONTH …) >= 6, which can't use an index on order_date.
LEFT JOIN … WHERE x IS NULL with the date condition in WHERE instead of ON, which turns it back into an inner join.

followups.question: Rewrite it as LEFT JOIN anti-join.
followups.answer: LEFT JOIN the recent order lines (date condition in ON) and keep rows where the joined id IS NULL.

followups.question: How would you check the plan?
followups.answer: Run EXPLAIN and look for Hash Anti Join or Nested Loop Anti Join.

followups.question: When is NOT IN safe?
followups.answer: When the subquery column is NOT NULL (or you add WHERE col IS NOT NULL).

takeaway: Prefer NOT EXISTS for 'has no matching row': NULL-safe and planned as an anti-join.
